core_claim: In America's prisons, the price of basics like ramen, deodorant, or a fan to survive the heat depends almost entirely on which state you're locked up in — and against wages of pennies an hour, that geography decides what basic dignity costs.

edt_01.label: Hook — The same ramen, four times the price
edt_01.title: The Same Ramen, Four Times the Price
edt_01.editorial_notes: Ramen $0.24 (NC) / $1.06 (FL) = 4.4x and deodorant $0.06/$2.90 = 48x must be exact. Note 46-of-50-state snapshot near this chart.

edt_02.label: The exchange rate is human labor
edt_02.title: The Exchange Rate Is Human Labor
edt_02.editorial_notes: 382 hours for a fan at $0.06/hr is the centerpiece number — do not round. Keep wage figures as 'roughly'; they come from det_02, not the dataset.

edt_03.label: The price of staying cool
edt_03.title: The Price of Staying Cool
edt_03.editorial_notes: Fan $10.02 (WY) to $43.80 (NV). Tie to heat/no-AC framing from det_06.

edt_04.label: What costs the most is faith
edt_04.title: What Costs the Most Is Faith
edt_04.editorial_notes: Quran $25.99 vs Bible $5.21 must be exact. Acknowledge small samples for religious items lightly (use medians). This is the moral turn of the piece.

edt_05.label: Who sets the price
edt_05.title: Who Sets the Price
edt_05.editorial_notes: Keefe = 16 states; 29 of 46 outsourced. Michigan $0.93 vs Indiana $8.36 (9x). End on the geography-of-cost idea, not a summary.
